doc.title: John Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Saying no on Joe's behalf and choosing his engagements
summary: Levy has no trouble refusing low-paying college offers while Joe is easygoing; they now choose only worthwhile jobs and cruises.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Was that harder for you to do in the beginning? To say no, no, no? Or were you always—

No. It didn’t bother me to say no in a minute, you know. A lot of times, because Joe is very easy going. And he’d say, well you know. But I’d say, no, I don’t want to do that. See but if you insist, you know, if you really want to do it. But this is the deal, if you really want to go on and do it. And a lot of times he’ll say, well I’ll go on, you know. We had a lot of offers to play with different college jazz bands all around the country. So that would mean just Joe and Norman would come in. And they would say this is the price or the conditions and everything, or, “we’re just a school starting out” or, “we have this band and we’re trying to raise money to keep it going” and all that nonsense. And I say, “yeah that’s nice,” I say, “but we’ve got to get this.”
Right. We’re making a living here.

Yeah. It doesn’t make any difference to me. And Joe would say, “yeah, we’ll go on and play it.” But now more and more he’s getting away from that, because, “it takes too much of my time. I have to go there, I have to rehearse with these guys, and take up the time, and as much as I like to try to help these schools and all that, I can’t do it anymore.” It’s too much. Joe’s 75 now you know. That’s—
Right. You’ve got to pick and choose.

Oh, you do, you do. And I, you know, really pick and choose the things that are most important for his career and for him, and the things he enjoys doing. It’s like these cruises. He enjoys cruises. Because he gets with the people and he mingles, he’s very open, and he enjoys being around people. But I turned down several other cruises, you know I’ve turned them down. I only pick the best ones, and go out on that and everything. And he talks about your school — he loves Hamilton. And I think he was there for George Shearing.
